'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]]
**[[Belarus–Russia relations]]
***[[Russia]] and [[Belarus]] begin a 10-day [[military exercise]] known as "Allied Resolve-2022" amid ongoing tensions with [[Ukraine]]. The [[United States]] and [[NATO]] denounce the exercise, with NATO calling it the biggest deployment of Russian troops since the [[Cold War]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2022/02/10/russia-set-to-begin-massive-military-drills-with-belarus.html (CNBC)]
**[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
***[[Ukraine]] says that [[Russian Navy]] [[military exercise|drills]] in the [[Black Sea]] and the [[Sea of Azov]] have made navigation "virtually impossible", stating that the drills are part of a "[[hybrid war]]" against the country. Foreign Minister [[Dmytro Kuleba]] says that the Sea of Azov is completely blocked, essentially [[blockading]] Ukrainian ports. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-says-russian-drills-black-sea-made-shipping-virtually-impossible-2022-02-10/ (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-60340232 (BBC News)]
**[[Ukraine–United States relations]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] calls on any remaining [[Americans]] to leave Ukraine immediately due to increased threats of [[Russian military]] action. The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] issues a level 4 travel warning, the highest level. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-60342814 (BBC News)]
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**Four civilians are killed during a battle between [[French Army|French troops]] and [[Ansar al-Islam in Kurdistan|Ansar ul Islam]] in [[Burkina Faso]]. Ten [[militant]]s are killed in the clash, which involved support from an [[attack helicopter]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/france-kills-10-islamist-militants-burkina-faso-2022-02-10/ (Reuters)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014-present)]]
** [[Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict]]
*** An airstrike on [[Abha International Airport]] in the [[Saudi Arabia]]n city of [[Abha]] injures twelve people. The attack was done by members of the [[Houthi movement]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/2/10/saudi-arabia-intercepts-drone-attack-12-injured (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] lifts its outdoor [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask mandate]] due to a decline in the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant|Omicron variant]]. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/world/821508/spain-drops-outdoor-mask-requirement/story/ (GMA News Network)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[Charles, Prince of Wales]], tests positive for [[COVID-19]] for the second time. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uks-prince-charles-tests-positive-covid-19-second-time-2022-02-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Western Australia]]
****[[Western Australia]] reports a record 37 locally transmitted cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-02-10/wa-records-37-new-local-covid-19-cases-plus-102-travellers/100818880 (ABC News Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
****The [[Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation]] proposes changing the definition of a fully [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinated]] person to only include people who have received a booster dose. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-02-10/fully-covid-vaccinated-two-doses-atagi-advice/100821406 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Costa Rica]]
***[[Costa Rica]]n [[President of Costa Rica|president]] [[Carlos Alvarado Quesada]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/costa-rican-president-tests-positive-for-covid-19/2499445 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
***[[Tunisia]] lifts its nightly [[curfew]] due to a decrease in the number of COVID-19 cases, but extends the ban on gatherings for one week. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/health-pmn/tunisia-lifts-covid-related-night-curfew-government (''National Post'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
* Aftermath of the [[Second Libyan Civil War]]
** The interim [[Government of National Unity (Libya)|Government of National Unity]], intended to be dissolved by the [[Next Libyan presidential election|2021 Libyan presidential election]] before its indefinite postponement, chooses former [[Ministry of Interior (Libya)|Interior Minister]] [[Fathi Bashagha]] to replace the incumbent, [[United Nations|UN]]-recognized Prime Minister [[Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh]], for his failure to hold the elections as agreed during the [[Libyan_peace_process|peace process]]. Dbeibeh rejects the appointment, saying that his replacement must be chosen by the eventual national election as per the aforementioned [[Libyan_peace_process#Military_track:_permanent_ceasefire|ceasefire agreement]], reigniting fears of renewed warfare. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/2/10/libya-tobruk-parliament-names-new-pm-fueling-divisions (Al-Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Archaeologist]]s announce the discovery of a [[human tooth]] in the ''Grotte Mandrin'' near [[Malataverne]], [[France]], dating to 54,000 [[Before Present|YBP]], around 10,000 years before the currently accepted date for the arrival of ''[[Homo sapiens]]'' in [[Europe]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/02/09/europe/tooth-human-neanderthal-france-cave-scn/index.html (CNN)]
